questions.question_text: Prove that $2\cot x\sec x = 2\operatorname{cosec}x$. Select the complete correct proof.

options.why: Replaced cotangent by tangent and then incorrectly identified the resulting fraction as cosecant.
Replaced secant by cosecant and then incorrectly simplified the resulting fraction.
Cancelled cosine but changed the remaining reciprocal of sine into sine.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{LHS} = 2\cot x\sec x$
$= 2\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}\dfrac{1}{\cos x}$
$= \dfrac{2}{\sin x}$
$= 2\operatorname{cosec}x$
$= \text{RHS}$

questions.question_text: Prove that $\dfrac{2(1 - \sin x)}{\cos x} = \dfrac{2\cos x}{1 + \sin x}$. Select the complete correct proof using the booklet's convention.

options.text: $\text{LHS} = \dfrac{2(1 - \sin x)(1 + \sin x)}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)} = \dfrac{2\cos^{2}x}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)} = \dfrac{2\cos x}{1 + \sin x} = \text{RHS}$.

options.why: Multiplied only the numerator by the conjugate, changing the expression.

options.text: $\text{LHS} = \dfrac{2(1 - \sin^{2}x)}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)} = \dfrac{2\sin^{2}x}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)} = \dfrac{2\cos x}{1 + \sin x} = \text{RHS}$.
options.why: Replaced one minus sine squared by sine squared instead of cosine squared.

options.text: $\text{LHS}^{2} = \dfrac{4(1 - \sin x)^{2}}{\cos^{2}x} = \dfrac{4(1 - \sin x)}{1 + \sin x} = \dfrac{4\cos^{2}x}{(1 + \sin x)^{2}} = \text{RHS}^{2}$, so $\text{LHS} = \text{RHS}$ without checking signs.
options.why: Equality of squares alone allows opposite signs; the argument omits the converse needed to establish equality of the original expressions.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{LHS} = \dfrac{2(1 - \sin x)}{\cos x}$
$= \dfrac{2(1 - \sin x)(1 + \sin x)}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)}$
$= \dfrac{2(1 - \sin^{2}x)}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)}$
$= \dfrac{2\cos^{2}x}{\cos x(1 + \sin x)}$
$= \dfrac{2\cos x}{1 + \sin x}$
$= \text{RHS}$

questions.question_text: Prove that $3\sec\theta - 3\cos\theta = 3\tan\theta\sin\theta$. Select the complete correct proof.

options.why: Omitted the extra cosine factor when converting the second term to the common denominator.
Reversed the subtraction and then incorrectly replaced cosine squared minus one by positive sine squared.
Replaced one minus cosine squared by sine rather than sine squared, losing a sine factor.

questions.question_text: Prove that $\dfrac{2}{\sin x\cos x} - 2\cot x = 2\tan x$. Select the complete correct proof.

options.text: $\text{LHS} = \dfrac{2}{\sin x\cos x} - \dfrac{2\cos x}{\sin x} = \dfrac{2(1 - \cos^{2}x)}{\sin x\cos x} = \dfrac{2\sin^{2}x}{\sin x\cos x} = \dfrac{2\sin x}{\cos x} = 2\tan x = \text{RHS}$.
$\text{LHS} = \dfrac{2}{\sin x\cos x} - \dfrac{2\cos x}{\sin x} = \dfrac{2(1 - \cos x)}{\sin x\cos x} = \dfrac{2\sin^{2}x}{\sin x\cos x} = 2\tan x = \text{RHS}$.
options.why: Omitted a cosine factor in the common numerator and then incorrectly replaced one minus cosine by sine squared.

options.text: $\text{LHS} = \dfrac{2(1 - \cos^{2}x)}{\sin x\cos x} = \dfrac{2\sin x}{\sin x\cos x} = \dfrac{2}{\cos x} = 2\tan x = \text{RHS}$.
options.why: Replaced one minus cosine squared by sine instead of sine squared and then confused secant with tangent.

options.text: $\text{LHS} = \dfrac{2(1 - \cos^{2}x)}{\sin x\cos x} = \dfrac{2\sin^{2}x}{\sin x\cos x} = \dfrac{2\cos x}{\sin x} = 2\tan x = \text{RHS}$.
options.why: Inverted the fraction during cancellation and then labelled cosine over sine as tangent.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{LHS} = \dfrac{2}{\sin x\cos x} - 2\cot x$
$= \dfrac{2}{\sin x\cos x} - \dfrac{2\cos x}{\sin x}$
$= \dfrac{2(1 - \cos^{2}x)}{\sin x\cos x}$
$= \dfrac{2\sin^{2}x}{\sin x\cos x}$
$= \dfrac{2\sin x}{\cos x}$
$= 2\tan x$
$= \text{RHS}$

questions.question_text: Prove that $\dfrac{2\operatorname{cosec}\theta + 2\sec\theta}{1 + \tan\theta} = 2\operatorname{cosec}\theta$. Select the complete correct proof.

options.why: Added the reciprocals with numerator one and then discarded the remaining sum factor.
Omitted cosine from the numerator's common denominator and then confused cotangent with cosecant.
Inverted the numerator fraction instead of the divisor, obtaining the reciprocal of the required result.

questions.question_text: Prove that $\dfrac{3}{1 + \cot^{2}u} + \dfrac{3}{1 + \tan^{2}u} = 3$. Select the complete correct proof.

options.why: Dropped the squares when taking reciprocals of cosecant squared and secant squared, then incorrectly assumed $\sin u + \cos u = 1$.
Replaced the denominators by the reciprocals of the correct identities and then incorrectly inverted each fraction.
Assumed both denominators equal one and then incorrectly added the two terms.

questions.question_text: Prove that $2\sec^{4}\theta - 2\tan^{4}\theta = 4\sec^{2}\theta - 2$. Select the complete correct proof.

options.why: Factored the difference of fourth powers as a squared difference, which omits the cross term.
Used tangent squared equals secant squared plus one instead of minus one, then changed the constant's sign.
Dropped the factor two after applying the Pythagorean identity and then asserted equality to twice the result.
